reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it announces a free Amazon and iTunes gift-card giveaway involving two $10 rewards, without requesting payment or private information. Subscription and comment milestones are presented as optional giveaway administration, and comments on the announcement do not count. The blurred code and changeable subscriber threshold are stated conditions, with no described payment demand, credential request, or deceptive destination.

citations.quote: [CLOSED] FREE iTunes and Amazon Gift Card Code Giveaway INFO
I have a ten dollar gift card for. Amazon and I also have ten dollars uh with iTunes credit that I'm going to give away
this giveaway is going to start once. I hit 1,500 subscribers
I'm going to have you guys subscribe to my channel, obviously,. And I'm going to have you guys only allowed to leave one comment
Comments on this video will NOT count towards the giveaway. You may subscribe now if you wish.

opening.argument: The promised gift cards are explicitly tied to audience actions, making this more than a passive announcement. The speaker says the giveaway begins only after reaching a subscriber threshold, then says participants will have to subscribe and leave one comment. The video therefore offers a low-barrier digital reward in exchange for channel engagement, while even early subscriptions are counted toward eligibility. That is a solicitation built around a promised asset, regardless of whether payment or private information is requested.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a payment request does not resolve the central concern: the reward is being used to obtain subscribers and comments. Calling those actions “administration” understates the explicit linkage. The title promises free gift-card codes, while the actual process is deferred to later videos and dependent on audience growth, leaving viewers to provide engagement before the promised giveaway is even launched.

citations.quote: [CLOSED] FREE iTunes and Amazon Gift Card Code Giveaway INFO
the winners. Is actually when I hit 2,000 subscribers

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The evidence shows an ordinary engagement-based giveaway, not an illicit claim process. The speaker describes two modest rewards and limits entry to one comment, which is a straightforward way to manage participation. The announcement also expressly says comments on this video do not count, so the cited description does not show that viewers are being induced to comment on the announcement itself. No payment, credentials, or external redemption step is identified.

citations.quote: I have a ten dollar gift card for. Amazon and I also have ten dollars uh with iTunes credit that I'm going to give away
Comments on this video will NOT count towards the giveaway.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a title promising free redeemable codes, a reward controlled by subscriber milestones, a possible early change to the threshold, and a code that is deliberately blurred. The speaker says the giveaway may end at 1,750 subscribers if growth is too slow, while also inviting subscriptions to count before the giveaway starts. This makes the conditions adjustable in the promoter's favor: viewers are asked to increase the audience for a reward whose timing and availability can change. The low-value prizes do not eliminate that deceptive structure.

citations.quote: [CLOSED] FREE iTunes and Amazon Gift Card Code Giveaway INFO

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account treats the stated conditions as reassuring, but those conditions are precisely the warning signs. A threshold that may move from 1,500 to 1,750, combined with a later winner announcement at 2,000, means viewers cannot rely on a fixed path to the reward. Blurring the code may protect it, but it also prevents viewers from independently verifying or receiving the advertised asset now.

citations.quote: I don't think I'll have a problem getting up to 1,500 in a short period of. Time
the winners. Is actually when I hit 2,000 subscribers

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These details do not establish deception. The possible threshold change is openly disclosed, not hidden, and the code is blurred because the speaker says it was more visible than intended. The speaker also says the physical Amazon card is ten dollars and describes the iTunes credit as something already won and being re-gifted. The evidence supports a small, imperfect giveaway with stated conditions, not a fabricated or unauthorized reward.

I won that in a giveaway so I'm just going to like re-gift. It, I guess.

opening.argument: Although presented conversationally as an update, this video functions as promotional recruitment. Its title foregrounds free gift-card codes, and the speaker directs viewers toward a sequence of future giveaway videos: first reaching a subscriber milestone, then entering through subscription and a single comment, and finally waiting for another milestone before winners are announced. The giveaway is therefore the mechanism for steering viewers into continued channel participation, not merely information about an already available reward. The promotional framing is reinforced by telling viewers that subscriptions made now will still count.

citations.quote: [CLOSED] FREE iTunes and Amazon Gift Card Code Giveaway INFO
When I actually post the videos,. Which I'll be sure to let you guys know

rebuttal.rebuttal: Describing the upload as an announcement does not make it non-promotional. The speaker postpones entry and winner selection until the channel reaches successive subscriber counts, then promises to notify viewers about later videos. That is a funnel from the free-code headline to ongoing channel growth. Saying viewers “may” subscribe does not change the fact that the reward is presented as a reason to do so.

citations.quote: So once I hit 1,500 subscribers, I'm going to post two different giveaways
I'm expecting 500 more subscribers. Until I announce it.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The announcement's promotional character is not evidence of a scam; ordinary giveaways routinely seek subscribers and manage entries through later posts. The speaker does not claim that this video itself is an entry form, and the description specifically says its comments will not count. The cited future milestones show timing and administration, but they do not show that the rewards are fictitious or that viewers must surrender money or sensitive information.
